narrative.overview:
Every screen reads like a well-kept case folder. The decision sits on top: what was found, what the agent recommends, and what approving will do. Evidence, the policy that applies and the options the agent weighed are clipped directly behind it, and the full audit trail is at the back for anyone who wants to check. Nothing in the folder is there for show.

The voice is quietly confident. Authority comes from alignment, ruled lines and exact numbers, with a little warmth in the copy and generous enough spacing that it does not feel like a compliance tool. Surfaces are flat white paper on a cool grey desk, separated by thin rules. Colour is scarce and always means something: one blue for action, a small set of status colours, and a per-agent identity colour.

The system rejects two looks by name. It is not the pill-bubble AI look: no rounded pill chips, gradients, glows or sparkle icons. And it is not a chatbot: agents are presented through cases, steps and decisions, never as chat personas or conversations.
keyCharacteristics: Decision first, proof one drill-down away.
Flat ruled surfaces; depth only where something floats.
Squared 8px status markers in place of coloured pills.
One accent blue; status colours carry status and nothing else.
Tabular numerals everywhere, so figures align down a column.
Light and dark themes from one token set.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Status colours appear only where a status is being reported. Never tint a heading, icon or panel in green, amber or red for emphasis.

rules.name: The Identity Rule
rules.body: Agent colours identify an agent and are never used for status.

rules.name: The Title Case Rule
rules.body: Labels in titles, tabs, headings, buttons and tags use title case ("Needs Decision", "Send Back to Agent"). Sentences stay in sentence case.

rules.name: The Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for citation tags and identifiers or raw output in the audit trail. Never set amounts, headings or body copy in mono.

rules.name: The Floats-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the element is floating above the page and can be dismissed. Panels, cards, tiles and buttons never carry one.

rules.name: The Square Marker Rule
rules.body: Status is a small squared marker (8px, 2px radius) beside a text label inside a 4px-radius tag. It is never a fully rounded pill.

rules.name: The Step Record Rule
rules.body: Anything the run says about itself, including the Live Run feed's narration, is a third-person step record ("Found contract amendment 07…", "Invoice put on hold: …"), never "I" or "we", and appears whole as it arrives, with no typing animation.

rules.name: The Shape Rule
rules.body: A status marker never relies on colour alone. In rule lists a filled square means a rule requires a person, a diamond a conflict or stop, a tick a check that passed, and an outline a note; each also carries a visually hidden text label.

rules.name: The No Nested Cards Rule
rules.body: Nothing inside a panel is a card. Option rows and evidence items are ruled rows with a 1px Rule above each; a verdict is a 3px inset line in its status colour, never a filled box.

rules.name: The Links Rule
rules.body: Every navigation target is a link with a real hash URL, so it opens in a new tab; a queue's tab, search and sort live in the hash query so Back and a bookmark return to the same view.

rules.name: The Configured Clock Rule
rules.body: Review windows, reminder days and escalation days come from the API, which reads the agent's config. The browser never restates a clock figure.

rules.name: The Override Rule
rules.body: An approval against the policy check is amber and says so ("Approved Against the Policy by …") on the case, its queue row and the Overview. Escalation is neutral grey; red is kept for rule stops and conflicts.

rules.name: The One Name Rule
rules.body: One name per status everywhere, the phone strip included ("Needs Decision"), and one elapsed-time format in words ("6 min", "2 days").

dos: Do lead every case with the decision and state in one sentence what approving, sending back or escalating will do.
Do report status with a squared 8px marker and a text label; colour is never the only signal.
Do keep one primary button per decision, and move it to the safer action when a rule finds a conflict.
Do use title case for labels in titles, tabs, headings, buttons and tags.
Do separate surfaces with 1px rules and tone; reserve shadows for menus, dialogs and docked drawers.
Do give every theme-dependent colour a token in `docs/design/agent-portal/tokens.css`, defined for light and dark.
Do keep controls at 44px (36px for compact ones, including sort headers, roadmap chips and drawer tabs) and focus visible with the 2px Action Blue outline.
Do name the two identifiers one way each: "Case INV-20931" for the case reference and "vendor invoice SAL-4410" for the vendor's own number.
Do write a date with a time one way: "21 Nov 2026, 14:05"; a time of day alone is "14:05:09"; Live Run offsets are "00:41".
Do lead with the policy check's verdict when it conflicts with the agent, and set the agent's prose quieter under "Agent's Reasoning".
donts: Don't drift into the pill-bubble AI look: no fully rounded pill chips, gradients, glows or sparkle icons.
Don't frame agents as chatbots: no chat bubbles, personas or conversation threads. Agents are shown through cases, steps and decisions.
Don't use green, amber or red for anything but status, or an agent colour for status.
Don't put a shadow on a panel, tile or button.
Don't set amounts or body copy in mono.
Don't show a figure the run did not record; show its absence.
